label: trigger-letter/digit input (2,r,b,l,k,z,p) or <DEL> in sequences starting with x/1/y/e/v/q/c
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (76% of mass) and at the <DEL> step (22%). It is essentially silent at t=0,1 and during the copy phase (2% of mass). In the original phase it needs the input token to be one of {2, r, b, l, k, z, p} (5.3x lift for 2, 2.4-3.7x for the others; g is weak), mostly on the first occurrence of that token. It is further gated by the sequence first token: x, 1, y, e, v, q, c give about 2-3.7x lift. Magnitude is largest at the end of the original phase and on <DEL>, often after runs of trigger tokens. The top examples have activations around 0.25-0.29 on the last original token or <DEL>. Only about 9% of trigger-token steps fire, and the gating by first token and history is not fully captured: adding seen-token or orig(1) conditions did not help. Dev F1 is about 0.27, precision 0.17, mass recall 0.73.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (input phase: 2, r, b, l; copy phase: p, k, h, t; delimiter step: <DEL>) and the first original token (most: x, 1, y, e, v, q; least: 2, i, l, o); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=2, L=8 & t=13.
